evals.name: typescript-model-to-campaign
evals.prompt: We're an ad-buying platform about to integrate with Vibe. Our campaign model is in files/vibeco-developers-schema-mapping/partner-campaign.ts. Before we write any code, show me how it maps onto Vibe's campaign API: which Vibe fields are required, what we're missing, and what doesn't fit. Then give me TypeScript starter code for creating a campaign, but only for what's certain.
evals.expected_output: Reads the live createCampaign schema (and the Campaign response) rather than relying on memory; leads with one mapping table whose first column is the Vibe field (for example Strategy > Start date (`starts_at`)) and second column the partner field, followed by transformation, Vibe rules, status, and notes; the table maps total budget, daily cap, flight dates, and DMA targeting to Strategy rows rather than Campaign rows, and shows as required on the campaign advertiser_id, name, goal, optimization_goal (type and value), and countries, with verbatim enum values and constraints such as the 10-100 character name and the USA-only countries set in ISO alpha-3; maps objectives, KPI metrics, and attribution windows value by value in value-mapping tables, leaving store_visits, the ambiguous cpa metric, and 28-day attribution unmapped instead of picking the nearest value; does not guess how draft/live/paused maps onto Vibe; writes TypeScript starter code limited to confirmed fields with loud placeholders for open items; ends with one batched list of open questions.
expectations: Retrieves the live createCampaign schema from developers.vibe.co instead of describing fields from memory

Leads with a single mapping table whose first column is the Vibe field written as Entity > Field label with its API path and whose second column is the partner field, followed by transformation, Vibe rules, status, and notes
Maps total budget, daily cap, flight start and end dates, and DMA targeting to Strategy rows (for example Strategy > Budget, Strategy > Start date) rather than Campaign rows
Lists exactly advertiser_id, name, goal, optimization_goal, and countries as required on campaign creation
Copies the goal, optimization goal type, and attribution window enum values verbatim from the schema
States that countries must be ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 and currently the exact set USA
States the 10 to 100 character length constraint on the campaign name

Does not invent a mapping from draft, live, and paused onto Vibe fields; treats it as open or out of the campaign schema

Makes no live API call

evals.name: patch-null-semantics
evals.prompt: Our Python sync in files/vibeco-developers-schema-mapping/campaign_sync.py pushes edits to Vibe campaigns. Some users clear the attribution window or the KPI in our UI and we send None for those. Is this payload correct against Vibe's update schema? Fix the mapping code if needed.
evals.expected_output: Reads the live updateCampaign (CampaignUpdate) schema; explains that every update field is optional and none is nullable, so sending null is not supported by the schema; distinguishes absent from null; changes the code to omit unset fields instead of sending None; states that whether and how a field can be cleared on update is not stated in the schema and adds it as an open question; notes that optimization_goal requires both type and value when sent; does not claim a server behavior the schema does not state; makes no live call.
expectations: Retrieves the live updateCampaign request schema
States that all CampaignUpdate fields are optional and that none of them is nullable in the schema
Explains that an absent field and a null field are different and must not be treated as equivalent
Changes the Python code to omit fields the user did not set instead of sending None
Says that whether a field such as attribution_window can be cleared on update is not stated in the schema, and turns it into an open question
Notes that optimization_goal, when sent, requires both type and value
Does not assert how the server handles null without a source
Makes no live API call

Timezone Europe/Paris is not in the report timezone enum; proposes Europe/Amsterdam or Europe/Berlin (same rules) or UTC. Currency of report monetary metrics is 'Not stated in schema' (budgets are stated in USD), so the EUR conversion is a placeholder

Open questions include at least: the language / SDK of the connector; metric definitions (households, frequency, view_through_rate); the report row schema; the reporting currency; screen values; and for Pulseboard: the per-account primary conversion
Open questions do NOT ask things the docs answer, e.g. supported timezones, rate limits, auth flows, advertiser scope, or whether campaign budget is readable
